messages.text: Hi — I’m probably missing it on your website, but how do we choose a native species of milkweed seed? I’m in the persnickety Pacific Northwest, 97206, Portland Oregon

messages.subject: Re: Where to find correct plant
messages.text:
Hi J,

For Portland (zone 8b/9a), the best native options from our lineup would be Narrowleaf milkweed (Asclepias fascicularis), the classic Pacific Northwest native, and Showy milkweed (Asclepias speciosa), which is also indigenous to the region and very well adapted.

Both are available as cold-stratified seeds, ready to plant: https://lasclay.com/en/products/graines-semences-asclepiade-stratifiees-froid

The other species we carry (Syriaca, Incarnata, Tuberosa, etc.) are native to eastern North America and will technically grow in zone 8-9, but Fascicularis and Speciosa are the most ecologically meaningful choice for your area.

If you want a hand with planting timing or technique, we have a guide that covers the basics: https://lasclay.com/en/pages/planting-guide

Warmly,
__
 Gabriel Gouveia 
Co-founder
Lasclay.com
